presets.label: Sales increase 30%
presets.description: A sustained 30% demand lift, ramped in over 4 weeks.

presets.label: Sales drop 25%
presets.description: Demand falls 25% — how much stock is left stranded?

presets.label: A supplier fails
presets.description: No replenishment arrives for 8 weeks; in-transit stock is delayed, not lost.

presets.label: Port strike
presets.description: Every supplier lead time grows by 21 days for the whole horizon.

presets.label: Tariffs increase 15%
presets.description: Landed unit cost rises 15% with selling prices held — a margin squeeze.

presets.label: Cut prices 10%
presets.description: A 10% price cut, with demand responding at −1.2 elasticity.

presets.label: Push service level to 99%
presets.description: Raise the target fill rate and see what it costs in working capital.

lines.label: Working capital released
lines.basis: Sum over accepted purchase orders of (spreadsheet baseline units − units actually ordered) × the SKU's unit cost at the time. Baseline = cover p90 demand across the full lead-time + review window with no variance pooling.

lines.label: Stockouts avoided
lines.basis: Accepted purchase orders on SKUs that had an open or acknowledged shortage alert at the moment the recommendation was generated. Orders with no alert are not counted.

lines.label: Carrying cost avoided
lines.basis: Working capital released × the tenant's annual holding-cost rate, pro-rated over each order's protection window.

lines.label: Revenue protected
lines.basis: For each accepted order, the demand that stock on hand could not have covered over the protection window, valued at the SKU's selling price.

lines.label: Forecast improvement vs. naive
lines.basis: Weighted absolute percentage error of the model against a naive last-week-repeats baseline, over weeks that were forecast before they happened. No out-of-sample forecast weeks have matured yet.

body.caveat: Every figure is derived from decisions you accepted in this window and the inputs frozen on them at the time. Recommendations you never acted on contribute nothing.

findings.label: Gaps in weekly sales history
findings.why_it_matters: A missing week is not a zero-sales week, but the models cannot tell the difference. Gaps flatten seasonality and understate demand.
findings.how_to_fix: Re-export the full date range from your source system. If those weeks really had no sales, include explicit zero rows.

lines.label: Working capital released
lines.basis: Sum over accepted purchase orders of (spreadsheet baseline units − units actually ordered) × the SKU's unit cost at the time. Baseline = cover p90 demand across the full lead-time + review window with no variance pooling.

lines.label: Stockouts avoided
lines.basis: Accepted purchase orders on SKUs that had an open or acknowledged shortage alert at the moment the recommendation was generated. Orders with no alert are not counted.

lines.label: Carrying cost avoided
lines.basis: Working capital released × the tenant's annual holding-cost rate, pro-rated over each order's protection window.

lines.label: Revenue protected
lines.basis: For each accepted order, the demand that stock on hand could not have covered over the protection window, valued at the SKU's selling price.

lines.label: Forecast improvement vs. naive
lines.basis: Weighted absolute percentage error of the model against a naive last-week-repeats baseline, over weeks that were forecast before they happened. No out-of-sample forecast weeks have matured yet.

body.caveat: Every figure is derived from decisions you accepted in this window and the inputs frozen on them at the time. Recommendations you never acted on contribute nothing.
